newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds TSB 1996 pretax profit soars.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds TSB 1996 pretax profit soars.

text.p: Britain's largest retail financial services group, Lloyds TSB Group Plc, on Friday reported a 52 pct jump in pretax profits for 1996 to 2.505 billion pounds ($4.09 billion) and said it has "unique opportunities for future profitable growth."

The profit figure followed 1.650 billion the previous year which was the first full year following the merger between Lloyds Bank and TSB Group. It raised its dividend to 13.2p per share from 11p, while earnings per share soared by 63 percent to 31.2p from 21.3.

Lloyds said it made a restructuring provision of 75 million pounds ($122.4 million) following its purchase of the minority interest in Lloyds Abbey Life and expects to make cost savings of 50 million stg per year from the acquisition.
It also said it was raising its provision against possible redress from the mis-selling of pensions by 29 million pounds to 200 million.

In a joint statement, Lloyds TSB chairman and its new chief executive Peter Ellwood said the high quality of the bank's earnings should enable it to produce consistently higher returns than the industry average.
Lloyds TSB's total revenue rose seven percent to 6.75 billion pounds and net interest margin was maintained at end-1995 levels despite erosion in some areas. ($1=.6128 Pound)
